question: What is an indulgence in Catholic teaching?

choices.A: The remission before God of the temporal punishment due to sins already forgiven, granted by the Church using the merits of Christ and the saints
choices.B: A papal permission to commit a sin without it counting against you
choices.C: A guarantee of immediate entry into heaven upon death
choices.D: A cash donation to the Church that cancels all sins committed in a lifetime

teaching.title: Indulgences
teaching.body: An indulgence remits the temporal punishment (as distinct from eternal punishment, which is removed by absolution) due to sins already forgiven. The Church draws on the 'treasury of merit' — the superabundant merits of Christ and the saints. Indulgences may be partial or plenary (full remission). They were notoriously abused in the late medieval period, which sparked Luther's 95 Theses (1517). The Council of Trent condemned the abuses while reaffirming the doctrine. Paul VI's Indulgentiarum Doctrina (1967) reformed the practice and remains the current authoritative document.
